title: Indians Can Now Book Burj Khalifa, Sentosa Tickets Online Using UPI
excerpt: UPI payments are enabled for online bookings at At the Top, Burj Khalifa and Resorts World Sentosa attractions including Universal Studios Singapore, the Finance Ministry said.
body:
• Indian travellers can now use UPI apps to book online tickets for At the Top, Burj Khalifa in Dubai and for Resorts World Sentosa attractions in Singapore, the Finance Ministry said on October 30.
  • In Singapore the facility covers Universal Studios Singapore, the Singapore Oceanarium and Adventure Cove Waterpark, booked through Resorts World Sentosa.
  • Reader action: book Burj Khalifa on the official At the Top ticket site and Sentosa attractions on the official Resorts World Sentosa ticket page, and look for UPI among the payment options - the announcement covers these online bookings, not every purchase at the venues.
  • UPI is now accepted in 10 countries, and Uzbekistan is set to become the 11th, the ministry said.

Indian tourists can now pay with the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) when booking tickets online for At the Top, Burj Khalifa in Dubai and for major attractions at Resorts World Sentosa in Singapore, the Ministry of Finance said in a statement on Friday, October 30, reported by The Hindu BusinessLine. The change means a traveller planning a Dubai or Singapore trip can pay for these bookings from a UPI app instead of relying only on an international card.

What is covered, and who enabled it

The facility was enabled by NPCI International Payments Ltd (NIPL), the international arm of the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI), through partnerships announced on July 29 for the UAE and September 9 for Singapore, the ministry said. In the UAE, NIPL partnered with NEOPAY and Emaar Entertainment to enable UPI for online bookings at At the Top, Burj Khalifa, which the statement described as the first attraction in the UAE to implement UPI for e-commerce. In Singapore, NIPL collaborated with FOMO Pay to extend UPI acceptance to Resorts World Sentosa, covering Universal Studios Singapore, the Singapore Oceanarium and Adventure Cove Waterpark.

How to use it on a real booking

Start on the attraction's own booking site. For Dubai, the official At the Top, Burj Khalifa ticket page sells timed entry to the Level 124 and 125 observation decks, with tickets valid only for the date and time shown. For Singapore, the official Resorts World Sentosa tickets page sells Universal Studios Singapore day tickets and packages. At payment, choose UPI if it is offered for that booking and complete the payment in your UPI app, then keep both the payment reference and the issued ticket or booking confirmation. The Finance Ministry announcement did not specify transaction charges or the exchange rate applied, so check the final amount shown before you approve the payment.

Context: UPI abroad and Indian travel demand

The ministry said Singapore welcomed 1.2 million Indian visitors in 2025, underlining why Singapore was an early market for the expansion. UPI-based ticket booking for the Eiffel Tower in France was launched on January 26, 2024, it added. UPI is currently accepted in 10 countries - Singapore, the UAE, France, Mauritius, Nepal, Bhutan, Qatar, Sri Lanka, Cambodia and Greece - and Uzbekistan is set to become the 11th after a commercial agreement announced on August 30, 2026, during Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit to the country, the statement said.

What this does and does not change

The announcement is narrow, and travellers should read it that way. It enables UPI for online bookings at the named attractions; it does not say UPI is now accepted at every counter, shop or restaurant in Dubai or Singapore, and it does not remove the need for a card or other payment method elsewhere on the trip. For diaspora families hosting relatives from India, or India-based families planning a first Dubai or Singapore holiday, the practical gain is at the planning stage: two of the most-booked attractions on those itineraries can now be paid for before departure, in rupees, through an app the traveller already uses at home.
